our_title: MESHVERTGROUP shares bit 0x0010 with MESHFREEOTHR; meshFree frees interior vlbltab of grouped meshes
ran: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$INFRA/asan/lib (pristine) or $WORK/build/lib (patched); UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1; see repro/README. cd $WORK/repro/PS-SEP-1; $INFRA/asan/bin/mtst m16_lbl.msh -> '==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed: ... #1 _SCOTCHmeshFree mesh.c:132 #2 _SCOTCHmeshExit mesh.c:88 #3 SCOTCH_meshExit library_mesh.c:133 #4 main mtst.c:167' ('0x50b000000060 is located 32 bytes inside of 104-byte region'). Patched: $WORK/build/bin/mtst m16_lbl.msh prints statistics and exits 0; also on data/small2_lbl.msh and in 64-bit.
severity_note: Every labeled mesh file loaded by mtst/mcv/mord/gmk_msh/SCOTCH_meshLoad ends in an invalid free (abort with glibc); input is a user file but the file need not be malformed.
evidence: mesh.h:66 `#define MESHFREEOTHR 0x0010` and :68 `#define MESHVERTGROUP 0x0010`; mesh_io.c:147 `meshptr->flagval = MESHFREEVERT | MESHVERTGROUP;` with vlbltax inside the memAllocGroup of :159-163; mesh.c:130-132 `if ((meshptr->flagval & MESHFREEOTHR) != 0) { if (meshptr->vlbltax != NULL) memFree (meshptr->vlbltax + meshptr->baseval);`.
first_pass_critique: Status, mechanism and preferred option are right. 'Not compiled' is now done: every user of the flags was checked (mesh_io.c, mesh_io_habo.c MESHFREETABS, hmesh_induce.c and mesh_induce_sepa.c FREETABS|VERTGROUP, hmesh_order_cp.c FREEVERT|VERTGROUP, library_mesh.c, library_mesh_order.c `&= ~MESHFREETABS`, hmesh.c:75); renumbering changes no other behaviour: hmeshExit's VERTGROUP test is reached only with FREETABS|VERTGROUP meshes, and library_mesh_order.c clears FREETABS before meshExit. The first pass did not notice that option 2 would also silence the vnumtab debug check and keep hmeshExit's test wrong.

fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit builds, 0 warnings; mtst on m16_lbl.msh and small2_lbl.msh clean under ASan; check_prog_mmk/mcv/mord/gmk_msh, check_scotch_mesh_graph, check_mesh_base pass in both builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Flag values are internal (mesh.h is not installed); no ABI change. Meshes with MESHFREETABS alone no longer 'have' VERTGROUP, which only matters for hmeshExit (no such Hmesh exists).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: This is what graph.h does (GRAPHFREEOTHR 0x0008, GRAPHVERTGROUP 0x0010, graph.h:84-86); one-line, same family as his 'assign proper variable' fixes.

our_title: meshBase skips load arrays; hmeshBase rebases halo end array with wrong range and double adjustment when aliased
ran: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$INFRA/asan/lib (pristine) or $WORK/build/lib (patched); UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1; see repro/README. cd $WORK/repro/SEP-23; ./base (pristine lib) -> 'check0=0' then '==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow ... #0 _SCOTCHmeshCheck mesh_check.c:199 #1 main base.c:22' (velotax read at the old base after meshBase (m, 0)). Patched: 'meshBase->0 old=1 check=0', 'meshBase->1 old=0 check=0', 'velotax[1..2]=2 3 vnlotax[3..6]=1 2 3 4', 'hmeshBase(alias)->0 old=1 check=0 alias=1', '...->1 old=0 check=0 alias=1', 'hmeshBase(distinct)->0 old=1 check=0 vehd=3 6', '...->1 old=0 check=0 vehd=4 7'. Same in 64-bit (bin64/base: 6 lines with check=0).
severity_note: Internal routines with no caller in the tree (latent); the review's 'info' understates that both routines corrupt memory when used (OOB read of load arrays, OOB write of vehdtax by baseadj entries when rebasing upwards).
evidence: mesh.c:175-182 shifts verttax/vendtax/edgetax/vnumtax/vlbltax but has no `velotax -= baseadj` / `vnlotax -= baseadj`; hmesh.c:106-112 `meshBase (&meshptr->m, baseval); for (velmnum = meshptr->m.velmbas; velmnum < meshptr->m.velmnnd; velmnum ++) meshptr->vehdtax[velmnum] += baseadj; ... meshptr->vehdtax -= baseadj;` (new range on old-based array; when vehdtax == m.vendtax the entries were already rebased by meshBase).
review_accuracy: accurate; its fix line ('shift all arrays and rebase vehdtax before looping') misses the aliased case: when vehdtax == m.vendtax, rebasing before looping still adds baseadj a second time to entries meshBase() already rebased, and leaves the pointer different from m.vendtax.
first_pass_critique: Status and tests right, and it did notice the aliasing. But its mesh.c sketch is wrong: velotax and vnlotax are two pointer fields, so shifting each once cannot 'shift it twice' even when both point to the same array (meshLoad); the 'shared load array' special case is dead complexity. Its hmesh.c sketch (vehdflag) is equivalent to the patch but keeps the loop body duplicated across the branches of the flag.

fix_options.label: Rebase every array consistently (graphBase idiom)
fix_options.summary: meshBase: shift velotax/vnlotax when non-NULL (as graphBase does, graph_base.c). hmeshBase: if vehdtax aliases m.vendtax, call meshBase and re-alias; else call meshBase, rebase the vehdtax access first, then add baseadj to the entries of the new element range. Add test_mesh_base (internal API, like test_fibo/test_common_thread).
fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit builds 0 warnings; repro/SEP-23/base all checks 0; check_mesh_base passes on both builds and fails on the pristine library with the same global-buffer-overflow.
fix_options.tradeoffs: No behaviour change for callers (none exist). Test uses internal headers like test_common_thread.c.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: graphBase() (graph_base.c:95-100) shifts velotax/vnumtax/vlbltax/edlotax; hmeshCheck() (hmesh_check.c:92) uses the plain `vehdtax != m.vendtax` alias test the patch reuses.

fix_options.label: Remove meshBase/hmeshBase
fix_options.summary: Delete both routines, their prototypes and module.h renames (no caller in src/).
fix_options.tested: syntax-checked only; `git grep -n 'meshBase\|hmeshBase' src` shows no other user.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Zero risk now; loses the mesh twins of graphBase() that SCOTCH_meshBase-style API could need later.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He kept graphBase() and exposes SCOTCH_graphBase(); deleting the mesh twins instead of fixing them is not his pattern (he fixed hmeshMesh's latent branch in f36ab36 rather than removing it).

ran: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$INFRA/asan/lib (pristine) or $WORK/build/lib (patched); UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1; see repro/README. cd $WORK/repro/API-12; ./bound 2 $WORK/scotch/src/check/data/small2.msh (SCOTCH_contextBindMesh then SCOTCH_meshGeomLoadScot on the container) pristine -> 'meshGeomLoadScot(container)=0' 'underlying mesh vnodnbr=0 check=0' + LeakSanitizer (mesh loaded over the container). Patched -> 'underlying mesh vnodnbr=7 check=0'. ./bound 3 (SCOTCH_meshExit on the container) -> no visible effect in either build (the container flag word has no MESHFREE bit); the guard mirrors SCOTCH_graphExit. meshOrderInit/meshCheck/meshSize on bound meshes (fixed part): check_scotch_context and the first pass's msh.c-style modes pass.
severity_note: The heap overflow of the lead (meshOrderInit) is fixed; the remaining routines write a mesh over the container (no overflow, sizeof(SCOTCH_Mesh) >= sizeof(Mesh)) and leak it, or read container bytes as a mesh (save/check of an empty mesh).
evidence: library_mesh_io_habo.c:82 `return (meshGeomLoadHabo ((Mesh *) meshptr, ...` while library_graph_io_habo.c:85 has `(Graph *) CONTEXTOBJECT (grafptr)`; library_mesh_io_scot.c:82 `meshGeomLoadScot ((Mesh *) meshptr,` and :100 `meshGeomSaveScot ((Mesh *) meshptr,`; library_mesh.c:133 `meshExit ((Mesh *) meshptr);` while library_graph.c:140 and library_dmesh.c:129 test `contextContainerTrue`.

our_title: Output graph handles of mesh/dmesh dual builders and graphDump's handle skip container unwrapping
read_only: SCOTCH_dmeshDgraphDual (library_dmesh_dgraph.c:78): read only; the patched library passes check_libparmetis_v3 (mpirun -np 3) but no test binds a Dgraph output.
severity_note: graphDump prints garbage/empty data (the first pass saw a stack over-read with a stack-allocated container); meshGraph into a bound graph leaks a whole graph and leaves the bound graph empty. The review's 'writes a whole graph over the small container' overstates: SCOTCH_Graph is at least as large as Graph.
